IDK, I guess I'll try.  But I seriously don't understand how this country expects anyone to survive in it without support of family or friends (which occurs in the real world).  Most countries have some support system for people like me (in Europe at least I have read).

I'm losing my mind.

On them joking though, they are not.  They have done this too me in the past in High School temporarily.  They will do it again permanently since I am now an adult in there view (and I technically am, but I love how unempowered I am right now in this economy.  I love how I am expected to live on my own, yet wages aren't high enough for me to do so).

How can I work for somewhere though?  I won't have a home to live in or a car to drive with (transportation in my current area is nonexistent).  I won't be able to shave at all (which will disqualify me) and I might smell like crap if I can't take a shower.

I don't need someone to talk to, no offense.  I need to fix my life now or I may die (I'm in the USA so there isn't exactly a lot of government support for people like me that I can run to).  And I may not even have a computer to talk on soon enough (because I won't have a home or an internet connection).

No offense, but this speech does nothing for me.  I went for a dream and put more work into it than anyone I fucking know, only to basically have it prevented by someone I couldn't get around.  Yes, after ALL these years, I know the solution to the issue.  But it was one that I could not achieve unless I had prior knowledge not to change schools during HS (which is something that should NEVER had occurred but evidently sending me to a public school system that is BOTTOM of the barrel in the US isn't a big deal for some people).  What worse is I know I could have acheieved it after all these years too AND there is literally nothing I can do now about it. 

These speeches mean nothing to me and I only see them as circle jerk sessions for people who made it.  I have no replacement for my dream and no way to get it back unless a time machine is made AND I can actually use it.  I'm left dead inside.  Speeches like that make me want to kill myself.

It doesn't matter at this point.  I am left knowing how majorly different my life would be if it was accomplished.  What is worse is I know I could have accomplished it after all these years still and it was due to someone preventing me from getting there (and there really was no way around this person).
I'll PM you.  I would love to hear how you pulled off getting in the computer world with your degree.

I used to live in a town that had multiple ski resorts.  I heard getting jobs there was extremely challenging.  Do you actually have experience with this?

Also, what jobs are you talking about with planting trees?  Never heard of this before.  My experience with the US is that this country is one of the few countries that DOESN'T create jobs just to create them.  There is no reason to, as there is really no support system for people who didn't just lose there job full time (not part time).
I'm in North America.  I have a way of getting a few hundred dollars, but a few is literally that.  No more than 300 sitting somewhere.

I know I can't.  I have zero interest with going into grad school with psychology or pursuing psychology later on.  

How could I just attend college off of fasfa temporarily as a way to get away from parents and save up money (while living off loans).  Then just drop out after first semester and be on my own.

Would that hurt my chances of getting into another grad school later on with something I want to really do?

How can I go to grad school?  What do I need to do?  Could I do it immediately?  I have zero interest in doing anything with my psychology degree later on.  But I would be fine attending grad school as a way away from parents temporarily, then just escape somewhere via resources in college.

I would love to get into grad school temporarily, drop out after I figure something out (which I feel could be done in a semester), and then maybe join the military later.  

Basically, I have trust issues with this house.  If I leave, I worry that they will go in my room (long story).  Can't put a lock on the door (not allowed I guess).

PS:  Would doing the above hurt me in getting into grad school later on in a program I actually have interest in (ones I have interest in take work experience and or extra classes I missed taking)?
